title: Build a Stage 8 Computing Showcase
overview: Bring together everything from Stage 8 Computing into one showcase: a working program, the data behind it, a clear explanation of how it runs, and the safety rules you followed while making it.

project.drivingQuestion: How can I use the computing I learned in Stage 8 to build something that solves a real problem for someone in my community — and explain exactly how it works?
project.finalProduct: A working program or digital product, the plan and algorithm behind it, a test-and-debug log, a data display, and a spoken or written explanation of your design decisions.

stages.title: 1. Plan and decompose
stages.prompt: Choose a real problem. Using the ideas from Units 1, 2, break it into smaller parts and write the algorithm before you write any code.
stages.evidence: A decomposed problem and a written algorithm or flowchart

stages.title: 2. Build it
stages.prompt: Build your program or product using the tools from Units 3, 4. Build the smallest working version first, then add one feature at a time.
stages.evidence: A working program or digital product

stages.title: 3. Test, debug and improve
stages.prompt: Test your work against your success criteria. Keep a log of every bug: what you saw, what caused it, and how you fixed it.
stages.evidence: A test-and-debug log with at least three entries

stages.title: 4. Share it safely
stages.prompt: Present your showcase. Explain three design decisions, show your data, and say which online-safety rules from Units 1, 2, 3, 4 you followed and why.
stages.evidence: A spoken, written or recorded explanation covering design, data and safety

evidenceChecklist: A decomposed problem with a written algorithm or flowchart
A working program or digital product
A test-and-debug log with at least three fixed bugs
Success criteria, each one ticked off with evidence
An explanation of your design decisions and the safety rules you followed

rubric.secure: The problem is decomposed, the algorithm is precise, and the pattern behind it is named.
The program runs, meets its criteria, and every bug found is logged with its cause and fix.
Data is collected accurately, organised sensibly and displayed so it answers a question.
Personal information is protected, sources are credited, and safety choices are explained.

questions.question: What does “Algorithm” mean in computing?
options: A set of ordered steps that are followed to solve a problem or complete a task.
A way of planning a program that is halfway between everyday English and real code; it has no fixed syntax.
A programming language, such as Python, designed to be easy for humans to read and write.
A named location in memory that stores one item of data, which can change while the program runs.
questions.answer: A set of ordered steps that are followed to solve a problem or complete a task.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Algorithm means a set of ordered steps that are followed to solve a problem or complete a task..

questions.question: What does “Assignment” mean in computing?
options: Storing a value in a variable, shown by <- in pseudocode or = in Python.
The name given to a variable, constant or sub-routine.
Choosing which code to run based on whether a condition is true or false.
A comparison test that gives a result of either true or false.
questions.answer: Storing a value in a variable, shown by <- in pseudocode or = in Python.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Assignment means storing a value in a variable, shown by <- in pseudocode or = in Python..

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: AND, OR or NOT - used to combine or reverse conditions.?
options: Boolean operator
Indentation
Linear search
Data type
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Boolean operator means aND, OR or NOT - used to combine or reverse conditions..

questions.question: What does “AutoValue” mean in computing?
options: A Base field property that numbers records automatically (used for a primary key).
One box in a spreadsheet, named by its column letter and row number, such as F7.
The address of a cell, such as B3, used inside formulas.
A rule a query uses to choose records, such as greater than or equal to 4.
questions.answer: A Base field property that numbers records automatically (used for a primary key).
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: AutoValue means a Base field property that numbers records automatically (used for a primary key)..

questions.question: What does “data” mean in computing?
options: Raw facts and figures, such as names, ages, prices and scores.
A tidy screen used to gather data one record at a time and store it.
An organised store of data that you can search, sort and update.
The Base field property that, set to Yes, makes a presence check.
questions.answer: Raw facts and figures, such as names, ages, prices and scores.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Data means raw facts and figures, such as names, ages, prices and scores..

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: One column of a table; all the data about one aspect of every record.?
options: field
fill handle
format
format check
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Field means one column of a table; all the data about one aspect of every record..

questions.question: What does “network” mean in computing?
options: A group of devices connected together so they can share data.
The physical parts needed to build a network, such as cables and routers.
Personal area network - a tiny network around one person's own devices.
Local area network - devices connected within one building or site.
questions.answer: A group of devices connected together so they can share data.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Network means a group of devices connected together so they can share data..

questions.question: What does “WAN” mean in computing?
options: Wide area network - devices connected across a large area, even worldwide.
Internet service provider - a company that provides an internet connection.
The shape or layout in which the devices in a network are connected.
A device that connects devices in a LAN and directs data to the right one.
questions.answer: Wide area network - devices connected across a large area, even worldwide.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: WAN means wide area network - devices connected across a large area, even worldwide..

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: A cable of copper wire that carries data as electrical signals.?
options: copper cable
fibre optic cable
interference
crosstalk
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Copper cable means a cable of copper wire that carries data as electrical signals..

questions.question: Which type of primary memory is volatile?
options: ROM
RAM
SSD
the CPU
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: RAM. RAM is volatile, so it loses its data when the power is off; ROM is non-volatile.

questions.question: Which is an example of system software?
options: a web browser
a game
an operating system
a word processor
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: an operating system. The others are all application software.
